context.exploration_scope: Real drift check (E40 fixed baseline) + 3 synthetic mechanism-verification tests (test_fixture_*, never real, never applied) proving the untested Gate/Execution/DEFERRED code paths are correct

problem: E37/E39/E41/E42 each only ever found 0 drift, so the Candidate Gate, the exactly-1-execution discipline, and the DEFERRED branch had never actually been exercised by any real data -- their correctness was unproven, not merely untriggered.

decision.decision_summary: Real drift check (E40 baseline): NO_NEW_EVOLUTION_FOUND (0 real changes) -- 0 real modifications, honestly. Separately, 3 deterministic synthetic tests (never real, never applied) proved: an executable discrepancy correctly yields exactly 1 candidate + 1 simulated modification; a non-executable one correctly resolves to DEFERRED with 0 modifications; a duplicate one is correctly rejected by the Gate. All 3 synthetic tests passed=true.

action.action_summary: Real fresh-read drift check against E40's fixed baseline (0 real drift, 0 real modifications) plus 3 synthetic, clearly-labeled tests of the Gate/Execution/DEFERRED logic -- no fabricated real finding, no real file touched by the synthetic tests.

result.note: The real project state has not changed since E40; the Gate/Execution/DEFERRED mechanism's correctness is now proven via synthetic tests rather than left unverified because real data never triggered it.

cause.root_cause_summary: A real discrepancy has not occurred since E40 to naturally exercise the Candidate/Execution/DEFERRED code paths -- proving their correctness therefore required deliberate, clearly-labeled synthetic verification rather than waiting indefinitely for real drift.

lesson: When a real system has remained genuinely stable, the honest way to verify an as-yet-untriggered code path is a clearly-labeled synthetic test that never touches real data or real files -- not fabricating a "real" discrepancy to force the path to run, which would corrupt the very record this whole arc depends on being trustworthy.
